Alex — thanks, pushing a short note below and attaching the spreadsheet. High level summary first: H100 is the best fit for Veridian's memory-heavy ensemble variants if you need native full-precision (or high-precision fp8+) and want predictable 95th-latency headroom for long-context ops. A100 is a good middle ground for cost-conscious steady throughput with moderate long-context memory (up to ~80–96GB effective with sharding/quantization). L4 is excellent for the short-chat workload (low-latency, high throughput, very low cost) but will require aggressive quantization and split-serving (offload large-model recency or embeddings to H100/A100).

Key recommendations (short):
- Reserve a mixed pool: primarily L4-backed slots for the short-chat burstable front-end (suggest 60% of reserved vGPU slots), H100 for pinned long-context/ensemble state (25%), A100 as an elastic mid-tier (15%) that can handle embeddings and overflow.
- Slot packing: use 1x H100 per large model instance (no overpacking), 2–4x L4 per hardware slot using containerized inference with continuous batching.
- Cache policy: prefix/KV cache for short-chat should remain on L4 instances; large-model KV stays on H100 to avoid repeated cold loads.
- Fallthrough: when reserved pool saturated, route low-latency chat to hosted L4 autoscaling endpoints (pay-as-you-go) with throttling; escalate embeddings to queued A100 workers. Avoid falling back large-model inference to CPU.

I attached an XLSX with token-per-dollar curves and a simple cost-sensitivity sheet. If useful, Dev can add a modeled headroom chart that maps expected 95th latency vs committed slots for each GPU class.

Rafael

Raf / Priya — I built the headroom matrix and included three scenarios in the attached sheet: conservative, nominal, and aggressive. A couple of technical notes that I think help Veridian decide:

1) Memory fragmentation cost: for ensemble models that require >96GB we recommend single-GPU H100 instances to avoid cross-GPU sharding at inference time; sharding adds both latency jitter and KV cache complexity. That means if any model variant exceeds ~96GB effective working set, count it as an H100 requirement.

2) Quantization runway: L4 yields the lowest TCO only if you can quantize to 4/5-bit without a significant quality drop; we included a simple eval delta column in the sheet. If Veridian's eval shows >3% quality regression on critical prompts, prefer A100 (fp16/4-bit mixed) or H100 for fidelity.

3) Packing heuristics: pack short-chat containers to 8–16ms batching windows on L4; continuous batching improves throughput without compromising 95th tail if you cap the batch-to-latency ratio.

4) Fallthrough policy (technical): implement a multi-tier route: reserved L4 -> reserved A100 -> reserved H100 (only for pinned jobs) -> hosted L4 autoscale. Use token-budget-based throttles to ensure critical short-chat gets priority.

I'll flag the sheet with the exact per-token price assumptions I used (includes reserved amortized cost, power, and NVIDIA support).
